_comment: Where each listed coin's daemon comes from, and what it costs to run.
Every repo and asset pattern here was resolved against the GitHub release
API rather than guessed — `provision.sh check` re-resolves them and fails
if a project has moved or renamed its artifacts.
`ramGb` is what the capacity guard enforces before anything is installed.
These are ESTIMATES from each chain's family and size, not measurements,
and they are deliberately not optimistic: the host also runs the exchange,
and an OOM there is customer funds becoming unreachable. `status` records
the real RSS once a node is up, which is how these become facts.
`rpcPort` AND `p2pPort` are both assigned here rather than taken from each
project's default, so two chains cannot silently collide on a port.
The RPC half of that was right from the start; the P2P half was not, and it
cost a daemon: Meowcoin and Neoxa are both Ravencoin forks and both default
their P2P listener to 8788, so whichever installed second died with
"Unable to bind ... is probably already running". A default shared by two
forks of the same parent is not an edge case on a list of small PoW coins,

XEL.name: Xelis
XEL.note: Its own RPC, not bitcoind-shaped. chains.ts has no adapter for it, so the exchange will keep reporting it unavailable until one exists — which is the honest state, not a gap to paper over.

ZEPH.name: Zephyr Protocol
ZEPH.note: Monero-family: the DAEMON serves chain data, and a SEPARATE wallet-rpc process holds the keys and issues subaddresses. Reconciliation needs only the daemon; deposits need both.

EPIC.name: Epic Cash
EPIC.note: MimbleWimble. No adapter in chains.ts either; same honest-unavailable state as XEL.

RXD.name: Radiant
RXD.note: NO RELEASE BINARIES — the latest tag ships source only. Left unautomated rather than pointing the installer at somebody's unofficial build of a chain we would hold customer funds on. Build it, then install by hand.

OCTA.name: OctaSpace
OCTA.note: An EVM chain, so a geth fork. The repo this was expected at returns 404, and it is also the most expensive node on the list — 8GB of RAM for a coin nobody has deposited yet. Confirm the real source before spending that.
